criteria.evidence: Bidirectional package/file, router/file, and consumer-dependency/file censuses; missing, duplicate, wrong-role, second-owner, undeclared-file, and mixed-owner fixtures.
criteria.outcome: Each `authored-markdown-v1` package has one authoritative Markdown and one generated XML. Markdown alone owns adopted content, stable IDs, and substantive metadata; XML contains only preserved semantics and classified envelope fields. Package, router, and consumer ownership closes bidirectionally.

criteria.evidence: Exact document-root, GFM/profile/XSD/converter, constructor/value-model, fragment/field/hierarchy/order census; root-digest, binding, insertion/deletion/reorder, duplicate-ID, ownership, unknown-field, unsupported-construct, and resource-limit fixtures.
criteria.outcome: Each package has one Markdown-owned document root and items with stable IDs, closed typed Pandoc content and metadata, hierarchy/order, authority binding, and typed-item digests. The GFM profile, XSD, and converter agree exactly on constructors, value models, fragment grammar, and envelope shape; XML-only, unknown, or unsafe semantics fail.

criteria.evidence: Exact normalized AST and parse-serialize byte comparison; minified, indent, tab, line-ending, namespace, attribute, empty-element, text-whitespace, add/drop/reorder, link/dependency, and manual-generated-edit fixtures.
criteria.id: SSM-MD-AC-03 — Conversion, readable XML, and back-render closure
criteria.outcome: Fresh conversion preserves the complete supported ordered Pandoc AST and emits XML equal to the readable storage law. The non-stored back-render preserves that AST after only listed normalizations; authored links remain content rather than inferred dependencies, and registered XML equals regeneration.

criteria.evidence: Cross-process conversion and independent item/field/XML/back-render/binding/dependency census; digest-invariance, missing, extra, duplicate, reordered, lossy, stale, self-report, second-owner, and stored-evidence fixtures.
criteria.outcome: Fresh readable XML is byte-identical across processes. Coverage independently recomputes every item/field, semantic path, authority binding, typed-item digest, back-render node, dependency, hierarchy, and order. Storage formatting cannot change semantic identity; converter self-report and stored evidence have no authority.

criteria.evidence: Exact edge/handoff and validation-read censuses; retained-control, nested-mutation, byte-equality, representation-isolation, handed-XML, default-control, reconversion, direct-read/reopen, conflicting-handoff, detached-token, undeclared-read, fallback, atomic-rollback/readback, and external-mutation fixtures.
criteria.id: SSM-MD-AC-05 — Snapshot-bound handoff, commands, and writes
criteria.outcome: Before model construction or writes, each declared edge constructs one handoff from a root-bound retained-byte snapshot after conversion, parser-control, typed-record, binding, back-render, and coverage validation. XML supplies validated generated bytes, paired with retained controls at model construction, and no prebuilt surface; Markdown supplies only authority bytes. Handed state is transitively immutable, and reopen, reconversion, detached tokens, inference, fallback, promotion, and pre-write-state reuse fail.

criteria.evidence: Exact contract/registry/schema/profile/converter/serializer/back-render/consumer/package/test census; storage-law, typed-field, whole-profile, XSD/profile, partial-update, control-bypass, reconversion-bypass, handoff-bypass, alternate-path, compatibility, and stored-record fixtures.
criteria.id: SSM-MD-AC-06 — Field evolution, audit, and implementation closure
criteria.outcome: An authored-field, storage-law, or typed-digest change coherently updates its Markdown owner, schema/profile, converter/serializer, back-render, coverage, consumers, and tests. Exact live closure has no production control bypass, alternate converter or generated-XML reader, consumer reconverter, mutable handoff, generated owner, untyped extension, consumer semantic field, stored evidence, compatibility path, or residue.
